clue.text: After Sprite, kid's given plum — it's this or nothing

parts.note: a hob is a hobgoblin, a sprite
a son is a child
plum means the best, choice

explanation.surface: After a fizzy drink, a child is offered a plum and told to take it or leave it.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprite looks like the lemonade brand; it is a mischievous spirit. Hobson was a Cambridge stable owner who let customers take the horse nearest the door or none.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobson's choice is an apparent option that is really no option at all: take what is offered or go without.

clue.text: Sitting at home, lying about going missing

parts.note: at home is in

indicators.note: what goes missing disappears, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: recumbent means lying down
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone lounging at home lies about having disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sitting' looks like seated; it means currently holding office, as a sitting MP.
explanation.definitionFit: The incumbent is whoever currently holds an office, just as a sitting member is the one in post.

clue.text: Group's second degree, not the last from Princeton

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is left out

parts.note: degree means extent, as in 'to some degree'

indicators.note: the last means the final position, so only the closing letter is taken

parts.note: final letter of the university's name

explanation.surface: A band member earns a second qualification but not the final one from an American university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degree' looks like an academic qualification; it means extent. 'Second degree' is a red herring phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a set of six musicians or things, a type of ensemble.

clue.text: One who's still growing a bouquet pockets hand-out

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: taken as written
a wine's bouquet is its scent
the dole is state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A florist's helper gets a tip tucked into a posy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' looks like flowers; it is the aroma of a wine. In Britain, the dole is unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager has not finished maturing physically, so is a youth still developing toward adulthood.

clue.text: Satisfied scripture from the east shows symbolic item

indicators.note: in an across answer, starting from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: a need is met when satisfied
Old Testament

explanation.surface: A contented scholar finds Eastern holy writings full of emblems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the east' sounds like Eastern religion; in an across clue it is a direction, right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or emblem venerated as representing a clan or idea.
